St Helena.notes: The 1966 edition contains a governor chain from 1836 to 1962. The existing chain ends at 1863 (Admiral Sir Charles Elliot, K.C.B.). All entries from 1863 onward are extracted below. Note: The 1966 edition lists year 1863 for Elliot which matches the existing chain endpoint. The 1964 edition has the same list but without years (bullet format). The 1966 edition includes years. The chain extends to Sir John Field (1962), who is listed as Governor and Commander-in-Chief in the Civil Establishment section of both the 1964 and 1966 editions.

Barbados.source: 1963_manual_parsed/barbados.txt lines 269-288 (primary, dated list); cross-referenced with 1966_manual_parsed/barbados.txt lines 317-336 (undated list with updated honours), 1899_manual_parsed/barbados.txt lines 153-171 (detailed 19th century entries), 1951_manual_parsed/barbados.txt lines 306-307, 1946_manual_parsed/barbados.txt lines 216-229
Barbados.notes: The 1966 edition contains a full governor list but WITHOUT dates for individual entries. The 1963 edition is the latest edition with a fully dated governor chain. The existing chain ends at 1865 (R. M. Mundy). The 1963 edition gives 1868 for Rawson while the 1899 edition gives 1866; the discrepancy may reflect different dating conventions (appointment vs arrival). The 1899 edition also includes many acting governors and administrators between the principal governors (Sanford Freeling 1875, George Dundas 1876/1878, D.J. Gamble 1880, R.W. Harley 1881, G.R. Le Hunte 1895/1897) which the later editions omit. The 1966 list ends with Sir John Montague Stow, K.C.M.G., K.C.V.O. (updated honours from 1963 edition). The 1958 edition just says 'see The West Indies (Federation)' — Barbados was part of the West Indies Federation 1958-1962.
